facts.label: Leverage and interest cover
facts.text: Reported-basis leverage is the figure to anchor on. Net debt excluding leases was 3.76x last-twelve-months reported EBITDA at 27 September 2026, against 2.75x at fiscal 2026 year end, because reported EBITDA over the last twelve months fell to CAD 277.8 million from CAD 362.7 million while total debt barely moved. Net debt rose by about CAD 49 million, mostly because cash fell by about CAD 54 million after CAD 61.3 million of share repurchases in the second quarter, and the company itself says the repurchases added about 0.1x to its leverage. facts.label: Liquidity and maturities
facts.text: Liquidity is not the constraint today. At 27 September 2026 the company held CAD 231.0 million of cash and had CAD 860.0 million undrawn on its CAD 900.0 million committed revolver, which matures in December 2029; it also states CAD 277.2 million more is available under letter of credit facilities, while CAD 274.4 million of letters of credit are outstanding. Literal checked analytical handoff, not native contract acceptance; source qualifications and gaps remain.

- The audited fiscal 2026 statements with notes, the annual MD&A and the auditor's reports are not supplied, so instrument-level carrying values, issuance costs, lease maturities, pension and contingency detail cannot be read; the statements printed in the results release are the only annual source. Severity High; the action that closes it is to obtain the annual statements exhibit. - Covenant levels, step-downs and definitions of the net debt to EBITDA and interest coverage tests are not printed, only a statement that all covenants were met at 27 September 2026, so covenant headroom is not calculable. Severity High; the action is to obtain the credit agreement or a compliance certificate. - The security and ranking of the two senior note issues and of the other credit facilities are not stated, so they are left out of the debt stack and of any secured or senior subtotal. Severity Medium; the action is to obtain the indentures or the annual information form. - The commitment status and expiry of the other credit facilities of CAD 111.6 million and of the letter of credit facilities are not stated, so only the revolver counts as undrawn committed, and the company's own unutilised credit figure of CAD 966.7 million is CAD 0.7 million below the sum of its stated components. Severity Medium; the action is to obtain the facility terms. - Carrying values by instrument and the unamortised issuance costs and premium are not stated, so the CAD 12.548 million difference between principal and carrying value is derived as a residual. Severity Medium; the action is to obtain the debt note of the annual statements. - The split of the CAD 274.4 million of letters of credit between customer advances, post-retirement obligations and leases is not stated, so the share that backs advances cannot be isolated. Severity Medium; the action is to obtain a schedule of letters of credit. - The completion date and net cash proceeds of the sale of two U.S. facilities, and the lease liability from the leaseback of one of them, are not stated, so the pro forma net debt rests on the CAD 71.2 million consideration. Severity Medium; the action is to obtain the third-quarter disclosure of the transaction. - The amount collected on the EV customer settlement in the first half of fiscal 2026 is not stated, so its effect on that period's operating cash flow cannot be isolated; last-twelve-months figures exclude it by construction. Severity Low; the action is to obtain the annual statements note on the settlement. - The repayment schedule of the CAD 150.0 million term facility and the maturity of CAD 4.2 million of other facilities are not stated, so their annual amortisation and ladder year are not supplied. Severity Low; the action is to obtain the credit agreement. - The undrawn committed facilities at 31 March 2025 and the principal total at that date are not supplied, because the credit facility was amended on 4 December 2025 and the exchange rate on that date is not in the supplied files. Severity Low; the action is to obtain the fiscal 2025 annual statements. - Cells the statements print as a dash are recorded as not supplied rather than zero: restructuring costs for the second quarter of fiscal 2026, impairment of assets, business acquisitions, swap settlements, purchase of non-controlling interest, repurchase of common shares and the IFRS 9 adoption amount in the cash flow statement, and assets held for sale at 31 March 2025; lines printed in only one of the statements are also recorded as not supplied in the other. Severity Low; the action is to confirm nil from the audited statements. - Closing cash for the first half of fiscal 2027 is not stated in the cash flow table because opening cash plus the net change differs from printed closing cash by CAD 1.158 million, an IFRS 9 initial adoption amount printed outside the three activities; the balance sheet shows the same closing cash. Severity Low; the action is to treat the balance sheet figure as controlling. - The company's pro forma adjusted EBITDA is not itemised, and its trailing figure of CAD 381.3 million differs by CAD 0.2 million from the constructed CAD 381.1 million. Severity Low; the action is to obtain the pro forma adjustment schedule. - Market revenue is reported on two definitions, and fiscal 2025 and 2026 are not restated to the fiscal 2027 markets, so the two series are kept apart. Severity Low; the action is to ask the issuer for restated fiscal 2026 market revenue. - Guarantor subsidiaries are not named and no restricted group is defined, so the perimeter of the guarantees cannot be mapped. Severity Low; the action is to obtain the annual information form.

facts.text: The strongest support is liquidity and visibility. facts.label: Financial profile
facts.text: The nine-dimension profile is assessed from the evidence above. Scale and market position is average: revenue of CAD 2,867.2 million over the last twelve months across several end markets, but no market share data. Competitive advantage is average, resting mainly on management statements about differentiated technology. Business diversification is average: four end markets, but life sciences is 51.43% of first-half revenue and customer concentration is not quantified. Cost and capex flexibility is average: capital expenditure is low and guided to CAD 60 million to CAD 80 million, yet the fixed-cost base is large enough to need a multi-year reduction program. Margin stability is weak because a revenue decline of 8.6% produced an adjusted EBITDA decline of 22.2%. Free cash flow stability is average: conversion is high but swings with working capital and one-off collections. Ability to refinance is average, helped by the extended facility and a first large maturity in December 2028, and limited by leverage above target. Liquidity position is strong. Financial policy and governance is average: deleveraging in fiscal 2026 is offset by repurchases above target and a control weakness. facts.label: Revenue durability and ownership
facts.text: ATS earns about 54% of adjusted revenue from construction contracts, which are project-timed and discretionary for customers, and about a quarter from services, which are steadier. Customers are primarily large multinationals, and customer concentration is named as a risk but not quantified, so revenue durability is average rather than strong. facts.text: Margins are exposed to operating leverage. In the second quarter gross margin fell to 28.5% from 29.9% and adjusted EBITDA margin to 12.1% from 14.2% on lower volumes and mix, while selling, general and administrative costs fell less than revenue. The program targets about CAD 65 million to CAD 75 million of annualised savings, with payback under a year, but lower revenues and mix are temporarily offsetting its benefits, so margins are more likely to defend through cost action than through volume in the next two quarters. facts.label: Industry forces and outlook
facts.text: Industry forces matter for credit mainly through buyer power and cycle timing. Buyers are large and decide timing of capital projects, so orders swing and revenue follows with a lag; supplier power is limited, as supplier lead times are generally acceptable and supply chain effects of trade changes have been largely mitigated through alternative sourcing and pricing. Evidence on rivalry, new entrants and substitutes beyond management's claim of differentiated technology is not in the supplied files, so those forces are not assessed. Political and trade factors are material: the USMCA review process and Section 338 tariffs delayed packaging orders in the second quarter. Exchange-rate factors also matter because the Canadian operations earn significant U.S. dollar revenue that exceeds the natural hedge. facts.text: Over the next 12 to 24 months the near-term outlook is for lower revenue, with third-quarter revenue guided below the prior year and earlier goals for growth and margin expansion no longer expected, and benefits from the program accruing over about 15 months. facts.label: Downside scenario
facts.text: The downside path starts with a further delay in non-life-sciences orders, for example if tariff uncertainty persists, so that third-quarter revenue lands below the guided range. The first operational break is fixed costs: in the second quarter an 8.6% revenue decline produced a 22.2% fall in adjusted EBITDA. As an analyst illustration anchored on the 15.54% first-half fall in adjusted EBITDA, applying that fall to last-twelve-months reported EBITDA of CAD 277.8 million gives about CAD 234.63 million, which lifts net leverage to 4.46x, or 4.15x pro forma for the facility sale, and lowers cash interest cover to 2.57x. Liquidity would still hold: the company would have cash of about CAD 231.0 million and CAD 860.0 million undrawn, although the revolver depends on covenant tests whose levels are not supplied. The consequence for refinancing is that the notes due in December 2028 would need to be refinanced with leverage above the target range, so a lender would look for restructuring savings to be visible in reported EBITDA first. Management levers are to stop repurchases, cut capital expenditure toward the bottom of the CAD 60 million to CAD 80 million range, accelerate the program and use the facility sale proceeds. The observable triggers are third-quarter revenue below CAD 640 million, the leverage measure above 3.1x, and any covenant disclosure. Resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress in this illustration, but not to hold leverage in its target range. Basis: calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C3; calculation C4; Financial foundation (CP-1); 6-K-EX-99.5_2026-09-27_ats-pressreleasexfy27q2.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4

facts.label: Overall credit view
facts.text: Overall, ATS presents an adequate business profile supported by scale across end markets, a life-sciences-led backlog and ample liquidity, but credit quality is constrained by earnings that fall faster than revenue, adjusted measures that rely on large add-backs, leverage above target and a financial policy that still includes repurchases. Cash-flow durability appears adequate but volatile because fiscal 2026 conversion rested on working capital and a one-off collection. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on leverage returning to the 2.0x to 3.0x range and on the restructuring savings appearing in reported EBITDA before the December 2028 notes. The primary downside path is a further order delay that cuts revenue below the guided range while fixed costs and add-backs persist. Further analysis would require covenant levels, the ranking and security of the notes, restricted payment limits and the audited annual notes. Fundamental credit view completed. Top risk: reported EBITDA falling faster than restructuring savings arrive while leverage is above target. ## Findings
### Bottom line

The seven supplied ATS filings support a credit snapshot through the quarter ended 27 September 2026, but only on management's own summaries of the debt terms, because no executed debt documents, audited annual notes or ratings were supplied. Creditors should read the leverage, liquidity and covenant findings that follow as company-reported and not independently verified.

spans.text: # CP-1 for ATS Corp /ATS (ats), as of 2026-11-05
## Request
ATS Corp /ATS (ats), as of 2026-11-05, credit snapshot pathway: financial foundation covering statements, debt, leverage, interest cover and liquidity from the supplied filings.
## Sources
| Source | Document | Document date | sha256 | Use |

| 40-F_2026-03-31_ats-20260331_d2.htm.jsonl | Annual report on Form 40-F of ATS Corporation for the fiscal year ended March 31, 2026 (cover, governance statements and exhibit index) | 2026-05-28 (signature date) | 461a9e1a5795ad26589158b15641a8ecb65a515f78e81e620080a11c1ee51f03 | Registrant identity and the exhibit index that shows the annual statements are not supplied |

| 6-K-EX-99.1_2025-12-28_ats-mdaxfy26q3.htm.jsonl | Management's discussion and analysis for the quarter ended December 28, 2025 (third quarter of fiscal 2026), furnished on Form 6-K | 2026-02-04 (date the MD&A is stated to be as of) | 495104fe5a368c3f86fa5f222fb1d1be8a8ff26e6c4af4a09766387bac60f769 | December 2025 Credit Facility amendment, 2025-03-31 facility comparatives, leadership changes |

| 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-03-31_ats-pressreleasexfy26q4.htm.jsonl | Results news release for the fourth quarter and fiscal year ended March 31, 2026, furnished on Form 6-K | 2026-05-28 | 9c0afcbd3db8908a2bce9809ae30cf6e21e3c8555f5c3d8e1a44911b7a679728 | Fiscal 2025 and 2026 statements, year-end net debt, EBITDA reconciliations, FY2026 balances |

| 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-06-28_ats-mdaxfy27q1.htm.jsonl | Management's discussion and analysis for the quarter ended June 28, 2026 (first quarter of fiscal 2027), furnished on Form 6-K | 2026-08-06 (date the MD&A is stated to be as of) | 7139467d52f7afd7dcfcd7f72f26d02042ad1d04d4e987664edd2eeedb7dac8a | First quarter of fiscal 2027 context and Credit Facility terms |

| 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-27_ats-mdaxfy27q2.htm.jsonl | Management's discussion and analysis for the quarter ended September 27, 2026 (second quarter of fiscal 2027), furnished on Form 6-K | 2026-11-04 (date the MD&A is stated to be as of) | 927254e506c477f0f3c479b731264614078302a7152fb02abbd056d0f3cf2206 | Latest debt terms, liquidity, contractual obligations, hedges, exchange rates, quarterly series |

| 6-K-EX-99.5_2026-06-28_ats-pressreleasexfy27q1.htm.jsonl | Results news release for the quarter ended June 28, 2026, announcing a Fixed Cost Transformation Program, furnished on Form 6-K | 2026-08-06 | bd6442bf8c1097adcf56b29d660c89aa138c0b9c5262ef32298dfe327594d94e | First quarter of fiscal 2027 adjusted EBITDA and program announcement |

| 6-K-EX-99.5_2026-09-27_ats-pressreleasexfy27q2.htm.jsonl | Results news release for the quarter and six months ended September 27, 2026, furnished on Form 6-K | 2026-11-04 | 678b14cb1aaa7e6f176b56c413e4c96ec51b564dcfbf0025fed22fc9c315392b | Latest statements, reconciliations, net debt, free cash flow, subsequent facility sale |
| Module | Handoff | sha256 | Use |
| CP-0 | Source readiness (CP-0), accepted | d2a15aca679e64d0f4bcbfe3f414acad02e0df4529931bc745af2c3a8ad3f234 | Source scope, document dates and gaps in the supplied set |
## Findings
### Bottom line

Net leverage on reported EBITDA has risen to 3.76x over the last twelve months to 27 September 2026 from 2.75x at fiscal 2026 year end, and interest cover has fallen to 3.05x from 3.72x, so creditors now depend on liquidity more than on earnings.
Basis: 6-K-EX-99.5_2026-09-27_ats-pressreleasexfy27q2.htm.jsonl, pages 17–21; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-03-31_ats-pressreleasexfy26q4.htm.jsonl, pages 12–18; calculation C12

Liquidity is ample, with cash of CAD 231.0 million and CAD 860.0 million undrawn on the committed revolver, and the first large principal maturity is the US dollar notes due in December 2028. The company's own 3.1x leverage relies on add-backs of CAD 103.3 million over the same twelve months, almost all restructuring and reorganisation costs, which must stop recurring for the adjusted view to hold. Covenant levels and the audited annual notes are not supplied, so covenant headroom is not established.

Basis: 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-27_ats-mdaxfy27q2.htm.jsonl, pages 24–28; 6-K-EX-99.5_2026-09-27_ats-pressreleasexfy27q2.htm.jsonl, page 14; 6-K-EX-99.5_2026-09-27_ats-pressreleasexfy27q2.htm.jsonl, page 17; calculation C11; calculation C13
### Leverage and interest cover

Reported-basis leverage is the figure to anchor on. Net debt excluding leases was 3.76x last-twelve-months reported EBITDA at 27 September 2026, against 2.75x at fiscal 2026 year end, because reported EBITDA over the last twelve months fell to CAD 277.8 million from CAD 362.7 million while total debt barely moved. Net debt rose by about CAD 49 million, mostly because cash fell by about CAD 54 million after CAD 61.3 million of share repurchases in the second quarter, and the company itself says the repurchases added about 0.1x to its leverage. Cash interest cover on the same basis fell to 3.05x from 3.72x. The cause is earnings, not borrowing: first-half revenue fell 7.21% and adjusted EBITDA fell 15.54%, so a further decline would erode cover faster than debt can be repaid.

Basis: 6-K-EX-99.5_2026-09-27_ats-pressreleasexfy27q2.htm.jsonl, page 17; 6-K-EX-99.5_2026-09-27_ats-pressreleasexfy27q2.htm.jsonl, page 2; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-27_ats-mdaxfy27q2.htm.jsonl, page 6; calculation C3; calculation C4; calculation C12; calculation C21

The company's headline looks steadier because it adds costs back. On adjusted EBITDA, net leverage excluding leases is 2.74x against 2.41x at year end, and the company's own 3.1x, which includes lease liabilities and its pro forma EBITDA, compares with 2.8x at year end and sits above its target range of 2.0x to 3.0x. The CAD 103.3 million gap between adjusted and reported EBITDA is 27.11% of adjusted EBITDA, and CAD 99.8 million of it is restructuring or reorganisation cost that management expects to continue for about 15 more months under the Fixed Cost Transformation Program. Until those costs stop, adjusted leverage understates the cash the business consumes.

Basis: 6-K-EX-99.5_2026-09-27_ats-pressreleasexfy27q2.htm.jsonl, page 4; 6-K-EX-99.5_2026-09-27_ats-pressreleasexfy27q2.htm.jsonl, page 14; 6-K-EX-99.5_2026-09-27_ats-pressreleasexfy27q2.htm.jsonl, page 17; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-27_ats-mdaxfy27q2.htm.jsonl, page 6; calculation C5; calculation C11; calculation C22
### Liquidity and maturities

Liquidity is not the constraint today. At 27 September 2026 the company held CAD 231.0 million of cash and had CAD 860.0 million undrawn on its CAD 900.0 million committed revolver, which matures in December 2029; it also states CAD 277.2 million more is available under letter of credit facilities, while CAD 274.4 million of letters of credit are outstanding. The next principal maturities are the US dollar notes in December 2028, CAD 494.9 million at the period-end rate, and the credit facility in December 2029, with CAD 190.0 million drawn, so refinancing is a task for fiscal 2029 and 2030 rather than now. The risk is access: the revolver sits under a net debt to EBITDA test and an interest coverage test whose levels are not supplied, so rising leverage could narrow what can be drawn before it narrows cash.
Basis: 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-27_ats-mdaxfy27q2.htm.jsonl, pages 24–29; calculation C13; calculation C14; calculation C15; calculation C24

The completed sale of two U.S. facilities for CAD 71.2 million after the quarter end would lower pro forma net leverage to 3.51x if the consideration arrives in cash and none of it is spent on the restructuring it is meant to fund. The completion date, the net proceeds and the lease liability from the leaseback of one facility are not stated.
Basis: 6-K-EX-99.5_2026-09-27_ats-pressreleasexfy27q2.htm.jsonl, page 11; calculation C17
### Cash flow quality

Cash flow over the last twelve months is weaker than fiscal 2026 suggests. Free cash flow from the statements was about CAD 259 million over the last twelve months and about CAD 37 million in the first half of fiscal 2027, against about CAD 372 million in fiscal 2026, which included a CAD 246.6 million release of working capital, and about CAD 150 million in the first half of fiscal 2026, which included collection of an EV customer settlement whose amount is not stated. Free cash flow was 0.93x last-twelve-months reported EBITDA, which is solid only because reported EBITDA is itself low.
Basis: 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-03-31_ats-pressreleasexfy26q4.htm.jsonl, page 18; 6-K-EX-99.5_2026-09-27_ats-pressreleasexfy27q2.htm.jsonl, pages 20–21; calculation C7; calculation C8

The working capital cushion is thinning. Non-cash working capital rose to 13.4% of annualised adjusted revenue from 12.1% at year end, and contract liabilities, the customer advances that fund projects, fell to CAD 290.8 million from CAD 307.3 million at year end and CAD 330.1 million at the prior year end. These advances are secured partly by letters of credit within the CAD 274.4 million outstanding, so if bookings slow the float unwinds and consumes cash while the letter of credit lines stay in use; the split of letters of credit by purpose is not stated. Provisions rose by CAD 6.7 million as restructuring costs were recognised ahead of payment, so a cash outflow is still to come.

Basis: 6-K-EX-99.5_2026-09-27_ats-pressreleasexfy27q2.htm.jsonl, page 17; 6-K-EX-99.5_2026-09-27_ats-pressreleasexfy27q2.htm.jsonl, page 19; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-27_ats-mdaxfy27q2.htm.jsonl, page 25; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-27_ats-mdaxfy27q2.htm.jsonl, page 29
### Definitions, one-off items and data quality

Four points of definition change the answer and are kept visible. The company counts lease liabilities in net debt; this analysis keeps them out of debt and shows CAD 146.5 million of leases separately, which is 0.53x of last-twelve-months reported EBITDA and would lift reported-basis net leverage to 4.29x. Fiscal 2025 reported EBITDA of CAD 162.0 million carries a CAD 171.1 million EV customer settlement charge against a revenue portion of CAD 146.9 million, so its 8.30x net leverage is not a run rate and adjusted EBITDA of CAD 368.9 million gives 3.65x. The company's trailing pro forma EBITDA of CAD 381.3 million differs by CAD 0.2 million from the constructed CAD 381.1 million because of rounding of one-decimal quarterly figures. The unutilised credit the company states, CAD 966.7 million, is CAD 0.7 million below the sum of its own components, and the CAD 111.6 million of other facilities in it has no stated commitment status.

Basis: 6-K-EX-99.5_2026-09-27_ats-pressreleasexfy27q2.htm.jsonl, page 17; 6-K-EX-99.5_2026-09-27_ats-pressreleasexfy27q2.htm.jsonl, page 23; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-03-31_ats-pressreleasexfy26q4.htm.jsonl, pages 12–13; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-27_ats-mdaxfy27q2.htm.jsonl, pages 26–27; calculation C18; calculation C19; calculation C20

Subsequent events are kept out of the period figures. After 27 September 2026 the company completed the sale of two U.S. facilities, on a day that is not stated, and a forward-starting swap fixes the rate on the CAD 150.0 million term facility at 3.264% from 4 November 2026 to 4 November 2028, which does not change debt. The statements are condensed releases without notes, the interim figures are unaudited, and printed dashes are recorded as not supplied rather than zero.
Basis: 6-K-EX-99.5_2026-09-27_ats-pressreleasexfy27q2.htm.jsonl, page 11; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-27_ats-mdaxfy27q2.htm.jsonl, page 30; 6-K-EX-99.5_2026-09-27_ats-pressreleasexfy27q2.htm.jsonl, page 20

## Gaps

- The audited fiscal 2026 statements with notes, the annual MD&A and the auditor's reports are not supplied, so instrument-level carrying values, issuance costs, lease maturities, pension and contingency detail cannot be read; the statements printed in the results release are the only annual source. Severity High; the action that closes it is to obtain the annual statements exhibit.

- Covenant levels, step-downs and definitions of the net debt to EBITDA and interest coverage tests are not printed, only a statement that all covenants were met at 27 September 2026, so covenant headroom is not calculable. Severity High; the action is to obtain the credit agreement or a compliance certificate.

- The security and ranking of the two senior note issues and of the other credit facilities are not stated, so they are left out of the debt stack and of any secured or senior subtotal. Severity Medium; the action is to obtain the indentures or the annual information form.

- The commitment status and expiry of the other credit facilities of CAD 111.6 million and of the letter of credit facilities are not stated, so only the revolver counts as undrawn committed, and the company's own unutilised credit figure of CAD 966.7 million is CAD 0.7 million below the sum of its stated components. Severity Medium; the action is to obtain the facility terms.

- Carrying values by instrument and the unamortised issuance costs and premium are not stated, so the CAD 12.548 million difference between principal and carrying value is derived as a residual. Severity Medium; the action is to obtain the debt note of the annual statements.

- The split of the CAD 274.4 million of letters of credit between customer advances, post-retirement obligations and leases is not stated, so the share that backs advances cannot be isolated. Severity Medium; the action is to obtain a schedule of letters of credit.

- The completion date and net cash proceeds of the sale of two U.S. facilities, and the lease liability from the leaseback of one of them, are not stated, so the pro forma net debt rests on the CAD 71.2 million consideration. Severity Medium; the action is to obtain the third-quarter disclosure of the transaction.

- The amount collected on the EV customer settlement in the first half of fiscal 2026 is not stated, so its effect on that period's operating cash flow cannot be isolated; last-twelve-months figures exclude it by construction. Severity Low; the action is to obtain the annual statements note on the settlement.

- The repayment schedule of the CAD 150.0 million term facility and the maturity of CAD 4.2 million of other facilities are not stated, so their annual amortisation and ladder year are not supplied. Severity Low; the action is to obtain the credit agreement.

- The undrawn committed facilities at 31 March 2025 and the principal total at that date are not supplied, because the credit facility was amended on 4 December 2025 and the exchange rate on that date is not in the supplied files. Severity Low; the action is to obtain the fiscal 2025 annual statements.

- Cells the statements print as a dash are recorded as not supplied rather than zero: restructuring costs for the second quarter of fiscal 2026, impairment of assets, business acquisitions, swap settlements, purchase of non-controlling interest, repurchase of common shares and the IFRS 9 adoption amount in the cash flow statement, and assets held for sale at 31 March 2025; lines printed in only one of the statements are also recorded as not supplied in the other. Severity Low; the action is to confirm nil from the audited statements.

- Closing cash for the first half of fiscal 2027 is not stated in the cash flow table because opening cash plus the net change differs from printed closing cash by CAD 1.158 million, an IFRS 9 initial adoption amount printed outside the three activities; the balance sheet shows the same closing cash. Severity Low; the action is to treat the balance sheet figure as controlling.

- The company's pro forma adjusted EBITDA is not itemised, and its trailing figure of CAD 381.3 million differs by CAD 0.2 million from the constructed CAD 381.1 million. Severity Low; the action is to obtain the pro forma adjustment schedule.

- Market revenue is reported on two definitions, and fiscal 2025 and 2026 are not restated to the fiscal 2027 markets, so the two series are kept apart. Severity Low; the action is to ask the issuer for restated fiscal 2026 market revenue.
- Guarantor subsidiaries are not named and no restricted group is defined, so the perimeter of the guarantees cannot be mapped. Severity Low; the action is to obtain the annual information form.

## Findings
### Bottom line

ATS is a publicly listed automation builder with no sponsor or controlling owner identified in the filings, so creditors depend on management's financial policy, which is in transition: a new chief executive, an interim finance chief, an unremediated control weakness and a restructuring program.

Basis: 40-F_2026-03-31_ats-20260331_d2.htm.jsonl, pages 7–9; 6-K-EX-99.1_2025-12-28_ats-mdaxfy26q3.htm.jsonl, page 3; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-27_ats-mdaxfy27q2.htm.jsonl, pages 36–38; 6-K-EX-99.5_2026-09-27_ats-pressreleasexfy27q2.htm.jsonl, page 4

Demand is mixed: second-quarter bookings of CAD 827 million rose 12.7% year on year but revenue fell 8.6%, and management no longer expects its fiscal 2027 goals of modest revenue growth and margin expansion. The company spent CAD 61.3 million on share repurchases in the quarter while its own leverage measure sat above its target range, and the sale of two U.S. facilities for CAD 71.2 million is meant to fund restructuring. Ownership percentages, guarantor entities and sponsor economics are not established.
Basis: 6-K-EX-99.5_2026-09-27_ats-pressreleasexfy27q2.htm.jsonl, pages 1–3; 6-K-EX-99.5_2026-09-27_ats-pressreleasexfy27q2.htm.jsonl, page 11; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-27_ats-mdaxfy27q2.htm.jsonl, page 6
### Key findings

ATS builds and services automated manufacturing systems, and its revenue is project-driven with a growing service share. Of fiscal 2026 adjusted revenue of CAD 2,970.1 million, construction contracts were 53.84%, services 24.37% and goods 21.78%, and life sciences was 51.24% by market and North America 52.48% by customer location. Services were 26.90% of second-quarter revenue and management expects recurring revenue of 25% to 35% on a trailing basis, which matters because service revenue is described as margin-accretive and less tied to customer capital cycles.

Basis: 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-03-31_ats-pressreleasexfy26q4.htm.jsonl, pages 11–12; 6-K-EX-99.5_2026-09-27_ats-pressreleasexfy27q2.htm.jsonl, page 9; 6-K-EX-99.5_2026-09-27_ats-pressreleasexfy27q2.htm.jsonl, page 13; calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C4; calculation C5

Demand has softened outside life sciences. Order backlog of CAD 2,009 million is 2.9% below a year earlier, and 61.62% of it is life sciences at CAD 1,238 million, while industrial and consumer backlog fell to CAD 312 million from CAD 431 million. Management attributes weaker non-life-sciences orders to timing and to tariffs that took effect in late August 2026 and were modified at the end of October to remove the effect on most covered products, and it guides third-quarter revenue to CAD 640 million to CAD 680 million against CAD 760.7 million a year earlier. Revenue therefore steps down before bookings can recover, so cash and leverage, not backlog, are the near-term constraint for creditors.

Basis: 6-K-EX-99.5_2026-09-27_ats-pressreleasexfy27q2.htm.jsonl, page 3; 6-K-EX-99.5_2026-09-27_ats-pressreleasexfy27q2.htm.jsonl, page 15; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-27_ats-mdaxfy27q2.htm.jsonl, page 31; calculation C6

Leadership and controls are in transition. The chief executive joined on 12 January 2026 and the chief financial officer's resignation took effect on 15 February 2026, since when the corporate controller has acted as interim finance chief. The company states that its disclosure controls were not effective at 27 September 2026 because of a material weakness in internal control over financial reporting first reported in fiscal 2026, and an ERP upgrade that went live in the quarter is still stabilising. For creditors the risk is the reliability of reported figures and of add-back classification while earnings fall.
Basis: 6-K-EX-99.1_2025-12-28_ats-mdaxfy26q3.htm.jsonl, page 3; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-27_ats-mdaxfy27q2.htm.jsonl, pages 36–38; 40-F_2026-03-31_ats-20260331_d2.htm.jsonl, page 3

Financial policy is partly creditor-aligned and partly not. The company brought its net debt to pro forma adjusted EBITDA measure down to 2.8x at fiscal 2026 year end from 3.9x a year earlier and extended its credit facility to 4 December 2029, but in the second quarter of fiscal 2027 it bought back CAD 61.3 million of shares at an average of CAD 27.32 per share while the same measure was 3.1x against a stated target range of 2.0x to 3.0x. Management says it expects to stay moderately above the range through fiscal 2027 and will pursue such uses only where there is a clear path back to range. The filings do not disclose the restricted payment limits that would cap further repurchases, so capacity cannot be separated from willingness.

Basis: 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-03-31_ats-pressreleasexfy26q4.htm.jsonl, page 15; 6-K-EX-99.1_2025-12-28_ats-mdaxfy26q3.htm.jsonl, page 20; 6-K-EX-99.5_2026-09-27_ats-pressreleasexfy27q2.htm.jsonl, page 2; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-27_ats-mdaxfy27q2.htm.jsonl, page 6; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-27_ats-mdaxfy27q2.htm.jsonl, pages 23–24

Restructuring is now continuous and sizeable. The Fixed Cost Transformation Program announced on 6 August 2026 targets annualised savings of CAD 65 million to CAD 75 million, about 250 basis points of margin and half of the 500 basis points still needed to reach the 15% long-term margin target. Implementation is expected to run about 15 more months with workforce reductions of several hundred including subcontractors, and CAD 21.3 million of restructuring was charged in the second quarter against nil a year earlier. The charges are added back to adjusted measures but are cash costs, and the sale of two U.S. facilities for CAD 71.2 million after the quarter end is intended to fund them.

Basis: 6-K-EX-99.5_2026-06-28_ats-pressreleasexfy27q1.htm.jsonl, pages 1, 3; 6-K-EX-99.5_2026-09-27_ats-pressreleasexfy27q2.htm.jsonl, page 4; 6-K-EX-99.5_2026-09-27_ats-pressreleasexfy27q2.htm.jsonl, page 11; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-27_ats-mdaxfy27q2.htm.jsonl, page 5

The filings name no sponsor, controlling shareholder or ownership percentage, so neither sponsor support nor sponsor extraction can be evidenced; the shares are listed on the TSX and NYSE and the audit committee has three independent directors. The debt was shaped by two placements of Canadian dollar notes due 2032 in 2024, US dollar notes due 2028 and a secured credit facility extended in December 2025, and guarantees come from subsidiaries that are borrowers or guarantors under the credit facility, whose names are not listed. Overall, ATS presents medium governance risk for creditors: the key supported behavior is share repurchases above the leverage target during a restructuring, which matters because it uses liquidity ahead of an earnings recovery, and the countervailing evidence is the fiscal 2026 deleveraging and the extended facility.

Basis: 40-F_2026-03-31_ats-20260331_d2.htm.jsonl, pages 7–8; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-27_ats-mdaxfy27q2.htm.jsonl, pages 26–28; 6-K-EX-99.1_2025-12-28_ats-mdaxfy26q3.htm.jsonl, page 20; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-03-31_ats-pressreleasexfy26q4.htm.jsonl, page 15
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest case against caution is operational and financial. Bookings rose 12.7% in the second quarter, life sciences backlog ended the quarter at the highest level in the company's history, the end-of-October change to tariffs removes the effect on most covered products, and the company states CAD 966.7 million of unutilised credit alongside a leverage measure that was 2.8x at fiscal 2026 year end. Management also expects restructuring payback in under one year. This view would win if revenue stays inside the guided third-quarter range and non-life-sciences bookings convert, which would let earnings recover without further share repurchases.
Basis: 6-K-EX-99.5_2026-09-27_ats-pressreleasexfy27q2.htm.jsonl, pages 1–4; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-27_ats-mdaxfy27q2.htm.jsonl, page 26; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-03-31_ats-pressreleasexfy26q4.htm.jsonl, page 15

A more positive view would follow leverage returning inside 2.0x to 3.0x, no further repurchases until it does, remediation of the control weakness and restructuring charges ending on the stated timetable. A more negative view would follow third-quarter revenue below CAD 640 million, a further bookings delay outside life sciences, repurchases or acquisitions while the measure exceeds 3.0x, or covenant levels that prove tight once disclosed.
Basis: 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-27_ats-mdaxfy27q2.htm.jsonl, page 6; 6-K-EX-99.5_2026-09-27_ats-pressreleasexfy27q2.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-27_ats-mdaxfy27q2.htm.jsonl, pages 37–38

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

The supplied filings report no new bond issue after December 2024; recent debt activity is the extension of the secured credit facility and use of the revolver. On 4 December 2025 the company amended the facility, moving maturity to 4 December 2029 and setting a CAD 900.0 million committed revolver and a fully drawn CAD 150.0 million term facility, with CAD 2.6 million of costs deferred and amortised. The notes outstanding are US dollar notes of USD 350.0 million due 15 December 2028 and Canadian dollar notes of CAD 600.0 million due 21 August 2032, the latter placed in two steps on 21 August 2024 and 19 December 2024, the second at a premium of CAD 1.3 million.
Basis: 6-K-EX-99.1_2025-12-28_ats-mdaxfy26q3.htm.jsonl, page 20; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-27_ats-mdaxfy27q2.htm.jsonl, pages 26–28

Other transactions bear on creditors. After 27 September 2026 the company completed the sale of two U.S. facilities for CAD 71.2 million, with an estimated gain of about CAD 12.2 million to be recognised in the third quarter of fiscal 2027 and an agreement to lease one facility back; a German facility remains held for sale. The transportation reorganization announced in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026 was completed in the second quarter of fiscal 2027, and the Fixed Cost Transformation Program, announced on 6 August 2026 with a European footprint consolidation as its first phase, is in progress. Heidolph and Paxiom were acquired before fiscal 2026, with about CAD 179 million of cash acquisitions printed for fiscal 2025 and none since.

## Request
ATS Corp /ATS (ats), as of 2026-11-05, credit snapshot pathway: fundamental credit synthesis built on the financial foundation and the business and governance facts.
## Sources

| Module | Handoff | sha256 | Use |
| CP-0 | Source readiness (CP-0), accepted | d2a15aca679e64d0f4bcbfe3f414acad02e0df4529931bc745af2c3a8ad3f234 | Source scope, document dates and gaps |
| CP-1 | Financial foundation (CP-1), accepted | 35e2707d5b7e1f0ca3030f5c88203478d7f91a7f2602eb21c80d87b4240f8a77 | Statements, leverage, cover, liquidity, maturities, post-balance-sheet adjustment |
| CP-1A | Business & governance (CP-1A), accepted | 4f4335754688e5ad5ea230a5ab73dc3caec783480f4eed6c1435b3d6f1215263 | Business mix, ownership, governance, capital allocation and events |
## Findings
### Bottom line

ATS is an adequate credit under pressure: reported earnings are falling faster than revenue, so net leverage of 3.76x, or 3.51x pro forma for the completed facility sale, depends on restructuring savings arriving before the 2028 notes mature.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 6-K-EX-99.5_2026-09-27_ats-pressreleasexfy27q2.htm.jsonl, page 4

Liquidity is the strongest support, with cash of CAD 231.0 million and CAD 860.0 million undrawn on the committed revolver, and no large principal falls due before December 2028. The weakest dimension is margin stability: the second-quarter revenue decline of 8.6% produced a 22.2% fall in adjusted EBITDA, and CAD 103.3 million of last-twelve-months add-backs separate reported from adjusted EBITDA. The sale of two U.S. facilities was completed after 27 September 2026 on a day the filings do not state. Covenant levels are not supplied, so headroom is not established.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 6-K-EX-99.5_2026-09-27_ats-pressreleasexfy27q2.htm.jsonl, pages 1–4; 6-K-EX-99.5_2026-09-27_ats-pressreleasexfy27q2.htm.jsonl, page 11
### Key findings

The strongest support is liquidity and visibility. Cash of CAD 231.0 million and CAD 860.0 million undrawn on the CAD 900.0 million committed revolver sit against near-term debt maturities of only CAD 2.4 million of bank indebtedness and a negligible current portion of long-term debt. Backlog of CAD 2,009 million, with 61.62% of it in life sciences, and second-quarter bookings that rose 12.7% give revenue visibility into fiscal 2027, although management guides third-quarter revenue to CAD 640 million to CAD 680 million, below the CAD 760.7 million of a year earlier.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 6-K-EX-99.5_2026-09-27_ats-pressreleasexfy27q2.htm.jsonl, pages 1–3; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-27_ats-mdaxfy27q2.htm.jsonl, page 31

The weakest dimension is margin stability. Second-quarter revenue fell 8.6% but adjusted EBITDA fell 22.2%, and the adjusted EBITDA margin fell to 12.1% from 14.2%, so fixed costs are not flexing with volume. Reported EBITDA is lower again: CAD 277.8 million over the last twelve months against CAD 381.1 million adjusted, because CAD 103.3 million of add-backs, CAD 99.8 million of it restructuring or reorganisation cost, is excluded from the adjusted measure. Creditors should underwrite reported earnings until the program's savings are visible.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 6-K-EX-99.5_2026-09-27_ats-pressreleasexfy27q2.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation C5

Net debt excluding leases is 3.76x last-twelve-months reported EBITDA against 2.75x at fiscal 2026 year end, or 3.51x pro forma for the sale of two U.S. facilities, which was completed after the quarter end on a day the filings do not state. Reported EBITDA covers cash interest 3.05x, down from 3.72x. On the company's own definition, which includes leases and pro forma EBITDA, leverage of 3.1x sits above its target range of 2.0x to 3.0x.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-27_ats-mdaxfy27q2.htm.jsonl, page 6; 6-K-EX-99.5_2026-09-27_ats-pressreleasexfy27q2.htm.jsonl, page 11

Cash flow is less durable than its conversion suggests. Free cash flow was CAD 258.6 million over the last twelve months and CAD 36.5 million in the first half of fiscal 2027, equal to 0.93x last-twelve-months reported EBITDA, but fiscal 2026 included a CAD 246.6 million working capital release and the first half of fiscal 2026 included an EV settlement collection. Contract liabilities, the customer advances that fund projects, fell to CAD 290.8 million from CAD 307.3 million at year end, so slower bookings would draw on cash.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-03-31_ats-pressreleasexfy26q4.htm.jsonl, page 18; 6-K-EX-99.5_2026-09-27_ats-pressreleasexfy27q2.htm.jsonl, pages 17, 20–21

Refinancing is a question for the next two years, not an immediate one. The US dollar notes of USD 350.0 million, CAD 494.9 million at the period-end rate, mature on 15 December 2028 and the credit facility, with CAD 190.0 million drawn, on 4 December 2029, so access on acceptable terms depends on leverage returning to the 2.0x to 3.0x range. The senior notes' security and ranking and the covenant tests are not supplied.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-27_ats-mdaxfy27q2.htm.jsonl, pages 26–28; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-27_ats-mdaxfy27q2.htm.jsonl, page 6

Financial policy is the swing factor. The company repaid debt in fiscal 2026 but bought back CAD 61.3 million of shares in the second quarter with leverage above target, has an interim finance chief and reports an unremediated control weakness. No sponsor or controlling owner is identified, so the board and management alone decide whether cash goes to creditors or shareholders, and restricted payment limits are not supplied.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-27_ats-mdaxfy27q2.htm.jsonl, pages 36–38; 6-K-EX-99.5_2026-09-27_ats-pressreleasexfy27q2.htm.jsonl, page 2
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest contrary evidence is that life sciences backlog and bookings are rising while tariffs have been eased, the company states CAD 966.7 million of unutilised credit, its own leverage measure was 2.8x at fiscal 2026 year end, and management expects restructuring to pay back within a year. This view would win if third-quarter revenue lands inside the guided range, the adjusted EBITDA margin recovers toward the 13.3% of the first quarter, and the facility sale proceeds fund restructuring so that net leverage returns to its target range without new repurchases.

Basis: 6-K-EX-99.5_2026-09-27_ats-pressreleasexfy27q2.htm.jsonl, pages 1–4; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-27_ats-mdaxfy27q2.htm.jsonl, page 26; 6-K-EX-99.5_2026-06-28_ats-pressreleasexfy27q1.htm.jsonl, page 4; Business & governance (CP-1A)

It would lose if third-quarter revenue falls below CAD 640 million, if add-backs persist beyond the roughly 15-month program horizon, or if covenant tests prove tight once disclosed. Conviction therefore moves on two observables: the leverage measure at the next two quarter ends and the pace at which restructuring charges decline. Further repurchases while leverage exceeds 3.0x would weaken the view.
Basis: 6-K-EX-99.5_2026-09-27_ats-pressreleasexfy27q2.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-27_ats-mdaxfy27q2.htm.jsonl, page 6; Financial foundation (CP-1)
### Limitations
Covenant levels and the executed debt documents are not supplied, so covenant headroom is not calculable and no view is taken on whether the revolver could be drawn in full.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-27_ats-mdaxfy27q2.htm.jsonl, page 27
No ratings, market prices or peer figures are supplied, so the assessment is not relative to peers or to market pricing.
Basis: Source readiness (CP-0)
The security and ranking of the senior notes are not stated, so the order of claims on the borrower is not established.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-27_ats-mdaxfy27q2.htm.jsonl, pages 27–28
Judgements on competitive advantage and customer concentration rest on management statements, because no market share or customer data are supplied.
Basis: 6-K-EX-99.5_2026-09-27_ats-pressreleasexfy27q2.htm.jsonl, page 9; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-27_ats-mdaxfy27q2.htm.jsonl, page 42

The downside illustration applies the first-half fall in adjusted EBITDA to last-twelve-months reported EBITDA as an analyst assumption; it is not a forecast and leaves out savings, working capital and interest changes.
Basis: calculation C1; Financial foundation (CP-1)
### Strengths and weaknesses

Strength one is liquidity. Cash of CAD 231.0 million and an undrawn committed revolver of CAD 860.0 million, with only CAD 2.4 million of near-term bank debt, mean the company can fund restructuring and working capital from available resources, which lowers the chance that earnings weakness becomes a liquidity event before the December 2028 notes.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-27_ats-mdaxfy27q2.htm.jsonl, pages 24–28

Strength two is the order book. Backlog of CAD 2,009 million, led by life sciences at 61.62%, and a trailing book-to-bill of about 1.05 times give partial coverage of revenue while non-life-sciences orders recover, which supports cash generation through the guided third quarter.
Basis: 6-K-EX-99.5_2026-09-27_ats-pressreleasexfy27q2.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 15; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C6

Strength three is a self-help program with funding. Annualised savings of CAD 65 million to CAD 75 million, about 250 basis points of margin, and CAD 71.2 million from the facility sale, which management intends to use for restructuring, address the fixed-cost base that is currently amplifying revenue declines.
Basis: 6-K-EX-99.5_2026-09-27_ats-pressreleasexfy27q2.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 11; Business & governance (CP-1A)

Strength four is a deleveraging record and a longer runway. The company's leverage measure fell to 2.8x at fiscal 2026 year end from 3.9x and the credit facility was extended to December 2029, which reduces refinancing pressure and shows past willingness to repay debt.
Basis: 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-03-31_ats-pressreleasexfy26q4.htm.jsonl, page 15; 6-K-EX-99.1_2025-12-28_ats-mdaxfy26q3.htm.jsonl, page 20; Business & governance (CP-1A)

Strength five is service content. Services were 26.90% of second-quarter revenue and management expects recurring revenue of 25% to 35%, which stabilises cash flow through the capital cycle if the share rises.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 6-K-EX-99.5_2026-09-27_ats-pressreleasexfy27q2.htm.jsonl, page 9

Weakness one is operating leverage. Revenue fell 8.6% and adjusted EBITDA 22.2% in the second quarter, so a further volume shortfall cuts earnings faster than revenue and pushes leverage and interest cover toward weaker levels.
Basis: 6-K-EX-99.5_2026-09-27_ats-pressreleasexfy27q2.htm.jsonl, page 4; Financial foundation (CP-1)

Weakness two is dependence on add-backs. The CAD 103.3 million gap between adjusted and reported EBITDA is 27.11% of adjusted EBITDA, so the company's own leverage of 3.1x understates the cash cost of its program for as long as charges recur.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C5

Weakness three is financial policy while leverage is above target. The CAD 61.3 million of repurchases in the second quarter used cash that could have reduced net debt, and the filings give no restricted payment limit that would stop repeat repurchases.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 6-K-EX-99.5_2026-09-27_ats-pressreleasexfy27q2.htm.jsonl, page 2; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-27_ats-mdaxfy27q2.htm.jsonl, page 6

Weakness four is reporting reliability. An unremediated material weakness in internal control, an interim finance chief and a new chief executive raise the chance that adjusted measures or accruals are later revised.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-27_ats-mdaxfy27q2.htm.jsonl, pages 36–38

Weakness five is cash flow volatility. Free cash flow moved from a CAD 52.3 million outflow in fiscal 2025 to an inflow of CAD 371.7 million in fiscal 2026 as the company states it, on working capital and a settlement, and the first half of fiscal 2027 produced only CAD 36.5 million, so debt service cannot be assumed from a single year's figure.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-03-31_ats-pressreleasexfy26q4.htm.jsonl, page 15; 6-K-EX-99.5_2026-09-27_ats-pressreleasexfy27q2.htm.jsonl, page 18
### Financial profile

The nine-dimension profile is assessed from the evidence above. Scale and market position is average: revenue of CAD 2,867.2 million over the last twelve months across several end markets, but no market share data. Competitive advantage is average, resting mainly on management statements about differentiated technology. Business diversification is average: four end markets, but life sciences is 51.43% of first-half revenue and customer concentration is not quantified. Cost and capex flexibility is average: capital expenditure is low and guided to CAD 60 million to CAD 80 million, yet the fixed-cost base is large enough to need a multi-year reduction program. Margin stability is weak because a revenue decline of 8.6% produced an adjusted EBITDA decline of 22.2%. Free cash flow stability is average: conversion is high but swings with working capital and one-off collections. Ability to refinance is average, helped by the extended facility and a first large maturity in December 2028, and limited by leverage above target. Liquidity position is strong. Financial policy and governance is average: deleveraging in fiscal 2026 is offset by repurchases above target and a control weakness.

### Revenue durability and ownership

ATS earns about 54% of adjusted revenue from construction contracts, which are project-timed and discretionary for customers, and about a quarter from services, which are steadier. Customers are primarily large multinationals, and customer concentration is named as a risk but not quantified, so revenue durability is average rather than strong. The order book converts to revenue over several quarters and includes long-duration enterprise programs in life sciences, which explains why revenue lags bookings in both directions; this makes the third-quarter guide, not the second-quarter bookings, the better indicator of near-term cash. Sales into the U.S. from Canadian and European operations are just over 20% of adjusted revenue and exposed to tariffs and the exchange rate, although management says tariff changes at the end of October remove the effect on most covered products.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-27_ats-mdaxfy27q2.htm.jsonl, page 29; 6-K-EX-99.5_2026-09-27_ats-pressreleasexfy27q2.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 12; calculation C4

Ownership is public with no sponsor or controlling shareholder identified, so there is neither sponsor support nor sponsor extraction to evidence; the debt sits with the listed company, guaranteed by subsidiaries that are borrowers or guarantors under the credit facility, whose names are not listed. Financial policy is therefore a board and management matter, set out in a leverage target range of 2.0x to 3.0x that management has said it will exceed through fiscal 2027.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-27_ats-mdaxfy27q2.htm.jsonl, pages 6, 27
### Margin resilience and cash conversion

Margins are exposed to operating leverage. In the second quarter gross margin fell to 28.5% from 29.9% and adjusted EBITDA margin to 12.1% from 14.2% on lower volumes and mix, while selling, general and administrative costs fell less than revenue. The program targets about CAD 65 million to CAD 75 million of annualised savings, with payback under a year, but lower revenues and mix are temporarily offsetting its benefits, so margins are more likely to defend through cost action than through volume in the next two quarters. The sensitivity to volume is the central credit risk.
Basis: 6-K-EX-99.5_2026-09-27_ats-pressreleasexfy27q2.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-27_ats-mdaxfy27q2.htm.jsonl, page 17; Financial foundation (CP-1)

Cash conversion is supported by low capital intensity: capital expenditure was about 2.65% of last-twelve-months revenue and is guided lower, and free cash flow equalled 0.93x reported EBITDA. Restructuring cash costs, cash taxes and lease principal sit on top, and working capital was close to neutral in the first half of fiscal 2027, which produced only CAD 36.5 million of free cash flow after restructuring and a CAD 25.8 million tax payment, so durable cash available for debt service is lower than conversion implies.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-27_ats-mdaxfy27q2.htm.jsonl, page 25; 6-K-EX-99.5_2026-09-27_ats-pressreleasexfy27q2.htm.jsonl, page 21
### Industry forces and outlook

Industry forces matter for credit mainly through buyer power and cycle timing. Buyers are large and decide timing of capital projects, so orders swing and revenue follows with a lag; supplier power is limited, as supplier lead times are generally acceptable and supply chain effects of trade changes have been largely mitigated through alternative sourcing and pricing. Evidence on rivalry, new entrants and substitutes beyond management's claim of differentiated technology is not in the supplied files, so those forces are not assessed. Political and trade factors are material: the USMCA review process and Section 338 tariffs delayed packaging orders in the second quarter. Exchange-rate factors also matter because the Canadian operations earn significant U.S. dollar revenue that exceeds the natural hedge.
Basis: 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-27_ats-mdaxfy27q2.htm.jsonl, pages 11, 14, 29–30; 6-K-EX-99.5_2026-09-27_ats-pressreleasexfy27q2.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 12

Credit-translated, strengths are scale across end markets, backlog, service content and a funded cost program; weaknesses are operating leverage, add-back dependence, repurchases above target and reporting reliability; opportunities are nuclear and radiopharmaceutical demand and tariff relief; threats are customer deferrals, further tariff changes and a failure to deliver savings on the stated timetable.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-27_ats-mdaxfy27q2.htm.jsonl, pages 8–9; 6-K-EX-99.5_2026-09-27_ats-pressreleasexfy27q2.htm.jsonl, page 3

Over the next 12 to 24 months the near-term outlook is for lower revenue, with third-quarter revenue guided below the prior year and earlier goals for growth and margin expansion no longer expected, and benefits from the program accruing over about 15 months. Over three to five years management points to nuclear refurbishment, radiopharmaceuticals and services as growth areas and keeps a 15% adjusted margin target; these support the credit case only if cost savings arrive and leverage returns to range before the 2028 notes mature.
Basis: 6-K-EX-99.5_2026-09-27_ats-pressreleasexfy27q2.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4, 7–9; 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-27_ats-mdaxfy27q2.htm.jsonl, pages 8–9
### Downside scenario

The downside path starts with a further delay in non-life-sciences orders, for example if tariff uncertainty persists, so that third-quarter revenue lands below the guided range. The first operational break is fixed costs: in the second quarter an 8.6% revenue decline produced a 22.2% fall in adjusted EBITDA. As an analyst illustration anchored on the 15.54% first-half fall in adjusted EBITDA, applying that fall to last-twelve-months reported EBITDA of CAD 277.8 million gives about CAD 234.63 million, which lifts net leverage to 4.46x, or 4.15x pro forma for the facility sale, and lowers cash interest cover to 2.57x. Liquidity would still hold: the company would have cash of about CAD 231.0 million and CAD 860.0 million undrawn, although the revolver depends on covenant tests whose levels are not supplied. The consequence for refinancing is that the notes due in December 2028 would need to be refinanced with leverage above the target range, so a lender would look for restructuring savings to be visible in reported EBITDA first. Management levers are to stop repurchases, cut capital expenditure toward the bottom of the CAD 60 million to CAD 80 million range, accelerate the program and use the facility sale proceeds. The observable triggers are third-quarter revenue below CAD 640 million, the leverage measure above 3.1x, and any covenant disclosure. Resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress in this illustration, but not to hold leverage in its target range.
Basis: calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C3; calculation C4; Financial foundation (CP-1); 6-K-EX-99.5_2026-09-27_ats-pressreleasexfy27q2.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4
### Overall credit view

Overall, ATS presents an adequate business profile supported by scale across end markets, a life-sciences-led backlog and ample liquidity, but credit quality is constrained by earnings that fall faster than revenue, adjusted measures that rely on large add-backs, leverage above target and a financial policy that still includes repurchases. Cash-flow durability appears adequate but volatile because fiscal 2026 conversion rested on working capital and a one-off collection. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on leverage returning to the 2.0x to 3.0x range and on the restructuring savings appearing in reported EBITDA before the December 2028 notes. The primary downside path is a further order delay that cuts revenue below the guided range while fixed costs and add-backs persist. Further analysis would require covenant levels, the ranking and security of the notes, restricted payment limits and the audited annual notes. Fundamental credit view completed. Top risk: reported EBITDA falling faster than restructuring savings arrive while leverage is above target.
